summary: The third rhythm: a 94-second silent film in eight shots, teaching from blocked light to an unresolved planet candidate within one continuous 3D world.
content:
Production grammar: One ThreeDScene, Cairo, 1280×720, 30 fps. Warm ivory stellar mesh; cyan b; violet c; amber candidate and unresolved evidence; gray excluded samples. Color identifies geometry, never certainty. Reserve top 17% for one formula and bottom 18% for at most two caption lines. Use 32–38 px captions, 42 px mathematics. All labels occupy these unobstructed bands, with leaders to active objects. Replace captions rather than accumulating them. Camera angles below are Manim phi/theta; smooth moves end in reading holds.

1 | 0–12 s — Ask backward.
At (65°,−55°), zoom 0.75, reveal the stellar sphere beneath a spatial constellation of seven small nodes at genuinely different depths. First two seconds: “The third rhythm” / “TOI-4342 · TIC 354944123”. Then root “A third planet?” Illuminate edges outward, successively naming “Repeated dimming”, “Orbit + sightline”, “Rule out impostors”; then leaves “Light + blocked area”, “Period + phase”, “Projection + inclination”. Each stage uses at most two caption lines; inactive nodes remain unlabeled. Repeated dimming connects to light and period; orbit connects to period and projection; impostor testing shares light and projection. Rotate theta −55°→−35° to expose these dependencies. End at the light leaf: investigation has reached familiar ground. Connections express prerequisites, not proof.

2 | 12–26 s — Light becomes area.
Travel to the same star, phi→0°, zoom→2.1, physical observer on +z. Restore accurate closeup sizes: stellar radius 1, planet radius 0.0337894036. Trace the candidate’s projected passage at impact parameter 0.74689457; the planet remains a 3D sphere on its foreground trajectory. Brief captions define “Transit: a planet overlaps the star along our sightline” and “Depth: the fraction of received light blocked.” Outline both silhouettes; show continuous partial overlap at ingress, then a fully interior disk. Exact main LaTeX: \delta\approx\left(R_p/R_\star\right)^2\approx0.001142. Hold with “Uniform-disk illustration” / “About 1142 parts per million”. Shading conveys shape, not photometric intensity. This derives an area approximation, not a measured light curve. Fade the equation before moving on.

3 | 26–39 s — A transit belongs to a sightline.
Pull back, zoom 1.05; phi 0°→65°, theta −35°→15°. Keep the physical observer marker and its white sightline stationary while the explanatory camera moves. Reveal the orbit’s depth and the planet when it passes behind the star; never delete the body. Captions, sequentially: “Sightline: the direction toward the observer” / “Projection: depth collapsed along that direction”; then “Inclination: angle between orbit normal and sightline” / “90° is edge-on”. Show one illustrative normal and angle arc. A faint orbit projection remains attached to the observer’s viewing plane; rotating around it reveals a circular spatial orbit and an elliptical projection. Final caption: “The orbit stays circular; its projection changes.” Omit directional belts and topology labels to preserve teaching time.

4 | 39–54 s — Three different clocks.
Pull back to zoom 0.75, phi→58°, theta→−45°. Reveal two solid orbit rings and one dashed amber ring labeled through the caption “candidate”. Use radii 1:1.55013194:2.26734965 and one clock driving angular speeds 1:0.51813986:0.29290194. First explain “Period: time for one circuit” / “Phase: position within that cycle”. Highlight each ring successively with exact numeric LaTeX labels: P_b=5.5382498\,\mathrm{d}, P_c=10.688716\,\mathrm{d}, P_{\rm candidate}=18.9082044035\,\mathrm{d}. Each replaces its predecessor. Display the distance line “Model-derived approximate distances: 0.05252 / 0.08141 / 0.11907 AU”. Final hold: “Circular orbits, phases and coplanarity illustrative” / “Overview body sizes exaggerated”. Distances use Kepler’s law and 0.63 solar masses. Preserve b/c’s original radii, 2.266/2.415 Earth radii, in construction metadata, consistent with [Tey et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2301.01370v1).

5 | 54–64 s — Remove known windows from the search.
Pan toward a spatial sample strand beside the still-visible system; theta→−25°, zoom 0.95. Caption: “Schematic brightness samples along time” / “Mask known b/c transit windows before searching”. Cyan and violet brackets select time intervals; selected beads become gray and move to a nearby excluded strand. Leave gaps in the retained strand: no subtraction, replacement samples or interpolation. Exact mask widths are unspecified. This makes exclusion visible before the residual search begins.

6 | 64–72 s — Recover the third rhythm.
Track retained beads toward three separated, equal-period cycle rings in depth. Hypothetical dimming markers align at the same phase as cycles overlay; their count illustrates repetition, not observed transit count. Main LaTeX: P_{\rm candidate}\approx18.9082\,\mathrm{d}. Captions: “A separate TOI-host search recovers this rhythm” / “Another search of existing data”. The amber orbital ring responds with a pulse but stays dashed. This illustrates phase alignment and the recovery reported in the [pinned repository](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eumemic/exoplanets/ec8311b19a61092ad5eae3d34e947b14485d363e/README.md).

7 | 72–86 s — Evidence has limits.
Orbit theta −25°→0°, zoom 0.9, toward the impostor branch. Eight evidence beads occupy staggered depths. First captions: “8 observing sectors; LEO reports 9 transits” / “13, 27, 66, 67, 93, 101, 102, 103”. Their positions encode no sky coordinates. Next, a schematic contaminating-light ray approaches the observer: “Nearest listed capable contaminator: 38.248 arcsec” / “Centroids do not fully localize the signal”. Remove it without a rejection checkmark. Final five-second hold replaces other text with LaTeX \mathrm{FPP}=0.11135>0.015 and captions “False-positive probability under tested models” / “Above the statistical-validation threshold”. This uses the updated ten-run Gaia-constrained result and [TRICERATOPS criterion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00691). No confidence gauge; low neighboring-source probability cannot settle target-associated alternatives.

8 | 86–94 s — Summary tableau.
Return toward the opening view over two seconds. Frame star, two solid rings, dashed candidate ring and unresolved root; evidence beads settle beside it. Hold “A candidate. Confirmation still needed.” Then retain that line while the second reads “Follow-up: ground photometry · high-resolution imaging · RVs”. End with three motionless seconds. The earned conclusion is an explained inference with an unresolved status. No official d designation, additional host or 47.5-day orbit; the latter belongs to the separate [ESPRESSO RV candidate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22115).

Implementation: Reuse a 16×32 stellar Surface, 8×12 planetary meshes, sampled curves and fixed dash segments; never rebuild surfaces per frame. Use set_camera_orientation/move_camera and fixed-frame overlays. Maintain physical planet positions through occultations; verify Cairo occlusion and silhouette scale in continuous playback. No render success or Jev approval is asserted.
checks: Read brief.json, mathematics.json and all six immutable source files; confirmed pinned commit and retrieval date.
Opened both requested primary papers, the pinned README and the TRICERATOPS primary paper; verified the separate RV candidate and validation thresholds.
Executed Python calculations: semimajor axes 0.05251722, 0.08140862, 0.11907490 AU; verified radius and angular-speed ratios.
Recomputed k² = 1141.72379867 ppm and ten-run FPP mean = 0.1113497766. Read sector IDs, nine-transit count, SNR values and centroid limitations directly.
Inspected installed Manim 0.20.1 metadata and Surface, Sphere, camera and fixed-overlay source APIs. Eight shot intervals total 94 seconds.
No files edited, repository changes, delegation or render attempted. Storyboard remains not_reviewed.
